_comment: Hand-reviewed mechanics layered over the research rows when build_depreciation_rules.py generates state_conformity.json. Use only for structure the research row states in prose but the generic mapping cannot express. Every override carries _why naming the research note it rests on. Never use this file to supply a figure without a source.

2021._why: batch1 note: CT adds back 80% of the federal 179 deduction and subtracts 25% a year over four years (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-701(a)(20); DRS excerpts).

2026._why: batch1 note: 30 Del. C. 1106(d)(1) - property acquired and placed in service after Dec. 31, 2025 continues under pre-OBBBA 168(k) (20% for 2026); property acquired earlier follows the federal rule.

2021._why: batch6 note: Ohio adds back 5/6 of federal 168(k) and of Section 179 above the amount allowed under the Dec. 31, 2002 law ($25,000 / $200,000), then deducts 1/5 a year for five years (2025 IT 1040 booklet lines 9 and 27). The 2/3 variant (withholding increase) and 6/6 (NOL year) are not modelled. The $200,000 phase-out is the 2002 federal figure, not stated by Ohio.
